 :JUDGMENT:

This Claim Petition is filed by the Petitioner against the Respondents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by him in the Road Traffic Accident.

2. The substance of averments made in the Petition is as under:
That on 31.07.2021 at about 7.45 p.m., the Petitioner being pillion rider and one Mahesh being rider of a Motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-02-JY-2015 were proceeding from Bengaluru to Govindayyanaplya, Kunigal Taluk on Magadi Main road and when they reached near Thippagondanahalli Village, Tavarekere Hobli, at that time the driver of the car bearing Reg. No.KA-02- MQ-4217 came from opposite direction to his extreme right side i.e., on wrong side of the road at high speed and in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner and caused the accident.
Due to the terrific impact, both rider and pillion rider fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately after the accident, the Petitioner was shifted to Lakshmi hospital, for first aid treatment and thereafter he was shifted to Apollo hospital, wherein he was treated as an inpatient.
Prior to the accident, the Petitioner was hale and healthy and he was working as Welder at Srikrishna Weld Tech, Gubbanna Industrial area, Bengaluru and was earning a sum of Rs.23,000/- p.m.
Due to the accident, he has sustained grievous injuries causing permanent disablement.
He has spent huge amount towards medical expenses, conveyance, nourishment and attendant charges.

The Respondent No.1 is the owner of the offending vehicle and the Respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle and therefore, both Respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the Petitioner.
Hence, this Petition.

Beeresh .G.K vs Rashe Pharma on 10 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/77412555/
2 3.
Despite of service of notice the Respondent No.1 remained absent and he was placed exparte.
In response to the notice the Respondent No.2 appeared before the Court through its Counsel and filed objections to the main petition.

In the Objection Statement, Respondent No.2 denied the age, avocation and income of the Petitioner and also denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending car bearing No.KA-02-MQ-4217.
Further, it denies the issuance of insurance policy to the offending Car subject to confirmation.
Further contended that the owner of the offending car has violated the Section 134(c) of MV Act.

Further it contended that the alleged accident has taken place only due to the negligence on the part of the rider of the motor cycle, he rode the same in a rash and negligent manner on a busy road that at 7.45 pm, unmindful of the traffic, resulting in the accident.
Further it contended that the quantum of compensation claimed is highly disproportionate and exorbitant to the facts and circumstances of the case.
Hence, it is not liable to pay any compensation.
On these grounds, Respondent No.2 has prayed to dismiss the petition against it.
4. On the basis of the above pleadings, my learned predecessor has framed the following Issues.
ISSUES 1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that he sustained grievous injuries in the nature of permanent disablement on 31.07.2021 at about 7.45 p.m. on Magadi Main road, near Thippa Gondanahalli Village, Bengaluru, in an accident arising due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of Car bearing Reg. No.KA-02-MQ-4217?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation? If so, how much and from whom?
3. What Order or Award?
5. In order to substantiate the case of the Petitioner, the Petitioner got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked 36 documents as per Ex.P.1 to P.35 and Ex.P.64.
He also got examined five witnesses as P.W.2 to PW.6 and got marked documents as per Ex.P-36 to P.63 and closed his side evidence.
On the other hand, Respondent No.2 has not chosen to lead evidence.

6. Having heard the arguments of the learned Counsel for the Petitioner and the learned Counsel for the Respondent No.2, upon perusal of the depositions, documents exhibited, citations relied by the learned counsel for the petitioner and materials available on record, my answer to the above Issues are as under:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No. 2 : In the Affirmative  Issue No. 3 : As per the Final Order  for the following :
 REASONS Beeresh .G.K vs Rashe Pharma on 10 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/77412555/
3 7.

Issue No.1 : It is the case of the Petitioner that he had sustained grievous injuries in the Road Traffic Accident that occurred on 31.07.2021 at about 7.45 p.m., due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of Car bearing No.KA-02-MQ- 4217.
8.

On the other hand, the Respondent No.2 has denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of Car bearing No.KA-02-MQ-4217.
9.
In order to prove the case of the Petitioner, he got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked 36 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P-35 and Ex.P.64.
P.W.1 has re-iterated the Petition averments in his chief-affidavit.
Ex. P-1
to Ex.P-5 are the true copies of FIR along with complaint, Spot panchanama with sketch, IMV report, Wound Certificate and Charge sheet.
Ex.P.6 to 8 are the notarized copies of SSLC marks card, Aadhar card and ID card of the PW.1.

Ex.P.9 is the Letter issued by Sri Krishna Weld Tech, Ex.P.10 is the Leave Certificate issued by Sri Krishna Weld Tech, Ex.P.11 is the letter issued by Sri Lakshmi Multi Specialty Hospital, Ex.P.12 is the Discharge summary of Apollo Hospital, Ex.P.13 is the Discharge summaries of Kanva Sri Sai Hospital (2 in nos.), Ex.P.14 is the Radiology report, Ex.P.15 is the Laboratory reports, Ex.P.16 is the Medical bills (63 in nos.) along with final bills, Ex.P.17 is he Advance receipts (15 in nos.), Ex.P.18 is the Prescriptions (11 in nos.),
Ex.P.19 is the X-rays (5 in nos.), Ex.P.20 to 34 are the Photos and Ex.P.35 is the CD.
Ex.P.64 is the Medical bills 14 in numbers.

10. Upon going through Ex.P-1 i.e., FIR with Complaint, same is evident that Tavarekere Police have taken statement of one Mahesh in Sri Lakshmi Multi Specialty Hospital and registered the case against the driver of Car bearing No.KA-02- MQ-4217 for the offences punishable under Sec.279,
337 of IPC.
Ex.P.2 is the true copy of Spot Mahazar with sketch.

The exact accident spot is marked in the annexed rough sketch which shows that the petitioner's bike was proceeding on its left side, the driver of offending car bearing No.KA-02-MQ-4217 came from opposite direction and changed his lane and came to his extreme right side and dashed against the petitioner's bike.

Ex.P.3 is the IMV Report, which shows that accident did not occur due to any mechanical defects of the vehicles and the damages found on the vehicles justify the involvement of vehicles and manner of the accident as narrated by the petitioner.
The Ex.P.4 is the true copy of wound certificate, which discloses that as a result of RTA, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

The charge sheet marked at Ex.P.5 discloses the fact that after thorough investigation IO has charge sheeted the driver of Car bearing Reg. No.KA-02- MQ-4217 for the offences punishable under Secs.279, 338 of IPC.
11.
In the cross examination, PW.1 has admitted that at the time of accident, one Mahesh was riding the motorcycle which belonged to Puneeth.
He further admitted that the said Mahesh had a driving license.
He admitted that there was no divider at the place of accident.
Further he admitted that there is a sharp turn at the place of the accident.
He admitted that in the hospital he had informed that the accident was caused by the car.
He denied the suggestion that due to the negligence riding of the rider of the bike the accident had occurred.

12. Further, petitioner has examined Medical record technician of Kanva Sri Sai Hospital, Bengaluru namely Smt. Vinoda B., as P.W.2 and got marked Ex.P.36 to 38 and Ex.P.59 to 63 i.e., Authorization letter, two case sheets, OPD record and Clinical assessment, Disability certificate, MRI report, Nerve Beeresh .G.K vs Rashe Pharma on 10 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/77412555/
4 conduction study report, Neuro Physiological assessment report along with worksheet.
These documents show that the petitioner was treated in the Nanva Sri Sai Hospital.
13. Further, petitioner has examined Dr.Avinash Parthasarathy, as P.W.3 and got marked Ex.P.39 to 46 i.e., O.P.D. slip, two disability Proforma and five X-rays records.

PW.3 is Orthopedic surgeon at Srinivasa Hospital, Bengaluru, re-iterated about the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in a RTA and assessed the disabilities of petitioner pertaining to Ortho related issues.

14. Further, petitioner has examined Account Manager of Sri Krishna Weld Tech, Bengaluru namely Sri Vinayak P. Naik, as P.W.4 and got marked Ex.P.37 to 54 i.e., Authorization letter, Appointment letter, Salary slips for the month from January to June.
He deposed that the petitioner joined their company as a welder in the year 2013.
They had been paying Rs.21,110/- gross salary per month to the petitioner.

15. Further, petitioner has examined M.R.D in charge of Apollo Hospital, Sheshadripuram,
Bengaluru, namely Smt.Voilet Mary, as P.W.5 and got marked Ex.P.55 to 58 i.e., Authorization letter, Inpatient case sheets, X-ray CD along with report and CT Scan CD along with report.
She deposed that the original MLC document has already been given to the police.
The doctor who treated the injured is still working in their hospital.
She admitted that she does not have personal knowledge about the treatment received by the injured.
16. Further, petitioner has examined Dr. Banu Prakash A.S., as P.W.6.
He deposed that petitioner is still under medication.
There is no specific treatment being given in respect of lambour plexus injury.

Further admitted that till the time patient had approached seeking assessment of disability,
the lambour plexus injury was not diagnosed.

He further admitted that Ex.P.11 discloses regarding the observations that 'bells palsy 6 years back and repeated 8 months back treated elsewhere and recovered'.
17.

The negligence aspect is concerned, though the respondent No.2 denies the negligent driving of the driver of the offending car, it has not examined driver of the offending Car to prove its contention.

On the other hand, as discussed above the spot Mahazar and rough sketch show that the driver of the offending car came from the opposite direction to his extreme right side and dashed against the petitioner's bike which was proceeding on its way.
This it self shows that the driver of the offending car had drove his car in negligent manner and caused the accident.
18. Furthermore the Respondent No.1 being the owner of the offending car despite service of notice has not appeared before the court and denied the negligence on part of his driver.
Moreover, the charge sheet is the material document, which has not been challenged by the driver of the offending vehicle.

Therefore, having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case and evidence adduced by the Petitioner and the documents exhibited, this Tribunal is of the opinion that, the Petitioner has proved that the said accident has occurred by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending Car bearing No.KA-02-MQ-4217 and in the said accident, the petitioner had sustained grievous injuries.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 is in the "Affirmative".

Beeresh .G.K vs Rashe Pharma on 10 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/77412555/
5 19.
Issue No.2 :
As the petitioner has proved that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of Car bearing No. KA-02-MQ-4217, as such the Petitioner is entitled for compensation.
20. In the petition, the Petitioner has shown his age as 28 years.

PW.1 has produced Ex.P.6 to 8 i.e.,
SSLC marks card, aadhar card and ID card to prove his age.
As per Ex.P.6 to 8, the date of birth of the petitioner is 03.06.1993.
The accident has taken place on 31.07.2021.
Hence, the age of the Petitioner, as on the date of accident was taken as 28 years and the same is to be taken for consideration.
21. Further, the PW.1 has averred that petitioner was working as Welder and earning a sum of Rs.23,000/-p.m.

In this regard, he has examined Account Manager of Sri Krishna Weld Tech as PW.4 and he has produced Appointment letter of petitioner and Salary certificates pertaining to the petitioner which are marked at Ex.P.48 to 54.
They justify that the petitioner was Welder in the said company.
The fact was proved by way of evidence of examination in chief of PW.4, he deposed that the petitioner was working as a Welder and was drawing a monthly salary of Rs.21,110/-.
The said witness in his testimony affirmed the fact that the petitioner was not able to continue the work with their company.
In the cross examination of PW.4 he admitted that in the salary certificates no mention about deduction of professional tax.
He further says their company pays the professional tax of all employees and no deduction of professional tax from the salary of the employees.

Hence,
the Tribunal believes the monthly income of or petitioner was Rs.21,100/- at the time of accident.
Therefore the income of Rs.21,100/- p.m. is taken for the purpose of assessment of compensation.
22. With this background, the quantum of compensation to which the Petitioner is entitled may be adjudicated.

For the sake of convenience, discussion may be had under following heads :
 I COMPENSATION TOWARDS PAIN, SHOCK AND SUFFERING:
23.
As per the Wound Certificate, the petitioner has sustained following injuries.
1.Degloving crush injury with bony exposure, tendon and ligaments exposure over right leg with frofuse bleeding and deeply contaminated wound.
2.Fracture right leg both bones-lower 1/3 of femur.
3.Puncture wound with bony deformity over right forearm upper 1/3-fracture right ulnar.
4.Blunt trauma over pelvis-public symphysis dislocation.
5.Multiple deep abrasions over bilateral upper extremities.
Beeresh .G.K vs Rashe Pharma on 10 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/77412555/
6 Wherein, the doctor has opined that the said injuries are grievous in nature.
Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that, awarding compensation of Rs.75,000/- under this head would be just and reasonable.

II COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF AMENITIES :
24.

The petitioner sustained loss of happiness physically and mentally, loss of amenities, loss of future earning capacity and prosperous, loss of future life span and also sustained pain and agony due to the injuries sustained by him.
The petitioner was deprived by his basic comforts and enjoyment.

Bearing in mind the nature of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of Rs.50,000/-
under this head would be just and reasonable.

III COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF INCOME DURING THE LAID -UP PERIOD:
25.

In this case the disability of the petitioner is considered at 100% and multiplier is applied accordingly, the loss of income during laid up period is not considered in lieu of petitioner is entitled for the compensation for 100% disability.

IV COMPENSATION TOWARDS EXTRA DIET & NOURISHMENT AND CONVEYANCE :
26.

As per Ex.P.12 and 13 discharge summaries, the petitioner took treatment as inpatient from 01.08.2021 to 10.08.2021, from 30.08.2021 to 11.09.2021 and from 21.12.2021 to 22.12.2021 for the total period of 25 days and the injuries sustained by him are grievous in nature.
The wound certificate also proves the same.

By considering the nature of injuries and period he spent to overcome pain and other allied affects of the accident and considering the treatment taken by the petitioner and injuries sustained he is entitled for compensation Rs.30,000/- towards food and nourishment, conveyance.
V. COMPENSATION TOWARDS MEDICAL EXPENSES :
27. The PW.1 has deposed that he spent huge amount towards medical expenses.
The petitioner has produced 63 medical bills at Ex.P.16 amounting to Rs.12,70,370/- and 14 medical bills at Ex.P.64 amounting to Rs.66,190/-, in total amounting to Rs.13,36,560/-.
There is no serious dispute about the medical bills.
Even the case sheets produced by the concerned hospital MROs also show that the petitioner has taken treatment in the aforesaid hospitals and incurred the expenses.
As such these medical bills are appears to be acceptable.

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.13,36,560/- which is rounded off to Rs.13,36,000/- as a compensation under this head.
Beeresh .G.K vs Rashe Pharma on 10 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/77412555/
7  VI
COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF FUTURE EARNINGS/COMPENSATION TOWARDS PERMANENT DISABILITY :
28. The PW.1 has alleged that due to the injuries sustained by the petitioner in the accident, he has suffered permanent disablement.
To prove the nature of injuries sustained by him and the disabilities, the petitioner examined Dr.Avinash parthasarathy as PW.3. and Dr. Banu Prakash as PW.6.
The PW.3 deposed that he is working as consultant Orthopedic Surgeon, he had examined the petitioner on 27.07.2022 for assessment of disabilities.
By that time the petitioner had complained about his difficulties due to the injuries sustained in the road traffic accident.
The PW.3 has produced O.P.D. slip, two disability Proforma and five X-rays which are marked at Ex.P39 to 46.

According to the evidence of this witness the petitioner sustained following injuries:
1. Fracture shaft of right femur,
2. Open type II fracture both bones of right leg,
3. Pelvic diastasis 4.
Right ulna fracture He further deposed that the petitioner underwent the following surgeries on 01.08.2021.
1. Wound debridement and Ex. Fix. Application for right leg.

2. CRIF with IM Nail for right femur,
3.Tibia realignment, debridement and VAC application.
PW.3 assessed total body disability at 30%.
29.
The PW.6 deposed that he is working as consultant Neuro and Spine Surgeon.
He further deposed that the petitioner had met with an accident on 31.07.2021.

Petitioner was unconscious till taken to hospital due to blood loss and severe pain with degloving crush injury to right lower limb,
upper limbs abrasions, he was taken to Sri Lakshmi hospital.

He was admitted in Apollo hospital,
underwent bone fixations fracture of pelvis sacrum, right femur, both bones of right leg, right ulna.

He further deposed that CT showed widening of anterior right sacroiliac joint., displaced fracture lower right sacral ala extending into sacral neural foramina medially and right sacroiliac joint with pre sacral hematoma.
Fat standing and fluid layering in the pelvis involving the retro peritoneum and perivesical space.
Decreased sensations and loss of power in right lower limb(p32,33).

30. As per Orthopedic surgeon-PW.3 the petitioner suffered 30% whole body disability due to permanent physical impairment in his right upper and lower limbs according to clinical and radiological assessment as per Govt. of India Gazette Notification guidelines.
According to the Neuro Surgeon-PW.6 the petitioner suffered 77% whole body disabilities.
As discussed above, the evidence of doctors show that the petitioner has to depend on others due to injury suffered by him.
The petitioner is wheelchair bound, he can stand with support with difficulty.
The said fact is established by the evidence of doctors and also medical records.
Further the photographs of petitioner marked at Ex.P.20 to 34 show the condition of petitioner.
It is pertinent to note here that,
the PW.1 was brought before the court on stretcher to adduce evidence and he has given evidence on laying position on the stretcher.
The said aspect is recorded by the predecessor in the office in the deposition of the PW.1.
This proves that he is bed ridden.
The age of the petitioner has to be considered to assess whether the petitioner can live independently without any one support.
Thus, it can be construed that the petitioner has to be depend on others and his avocational disability has to be considered at 100%.

In this regard, learned counsel for petitioner relied upon the following decisions;

She had suffered 'hypoxic ischemic brain injury', which results from damage to the part of the brain Beeresh .G.K vs Rashe Pharma on 10 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/77412555/
9 called cerebellum, which helps in coordination of muscle movement.
It also lead to slurred speech, apart from irregular and slow movement of the muscles.

As per the medical evidence, coming on record, she had suffered fracture right superior and interior pubic rami and fracture right femur with perineal laceration and she had undergone surgery on 10.09.2006 by the Gynecologist.

On account of 'fat embolism syndrome', on account of injuries, so sustained in the accident, she was further referred to PGI, Chandigarh, where she had also undergone operation for the fracture femur on 16.09.2006.

The injuries, as evident aforesaid, are permanent in nature, apparently, making the appellant-claimant, unfit for any employment.
Even though, the disability may be 83%, the kind of injuries, so suffered, make it absolutely impossible for a person to work and be gainfully employed.
Considering the nature of disability, there is bound to be loss of movement of all the four limbs and further having impact, upon the speech and also decrease in body functionality.
Considering this kind of condition of the appellant- claimant, even after such a long time of the accident, as such, the loss of income is held to be 100%.

Considering the educational input of the appellant- claimant, as per the educational certificates, coming on record as Ex.PX, PY and PZ and she being science student, preparing for P.M.T., in modest estimate, while relying upon Rahul Ganpatrao Sable vs. Laxman Maruti Jadhav, 2023 ACJ 1465 (SC),
wherein, reliance was further made on Lalan D. Vs. Oriental Insurance Company Limited, 2020 ACJ 2517 (SC), the income of the appellant is assessed to be Rs.20,000/- per month."

entities.text: M.R.Krishamurthi Vs New India Assurance Company Ltd.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Wherein the Hon'ble supreme court has held in para 22 as follows:
"We may now summarize the principles discussed above:
(i) All injuries (or permanent disabilities arising from injuries), do not result in loss of earning capacity.
(ii) The percentage of permanent disability with reference to the whole body of a person, cannot be assumed to be the percentage of loss of earning capacity.

To put it differently, the percentage of loss of earning capacity is not the same as the percentage of permanent disability(except in a few cases, where the Tribunal on the basis of evidence, concludes that the percentage of loss of earning capacity is the same as the percentage of permanent disability).

(iii) The doctor who treated an injured claimant or who examined him subsequently to assess the extent of his permanent disability can give evidence only in regard to the extent of permanent disability.
The loss of earning capacity is something that will have to be assessed by the Tribunal with reference to the evidence in entirety.

(iv) The same permanent disability may result in different percentages of loss of earning capacity in different persons, depending upon the nature of profession,
occupation or job, age, education and other factors."

In view of the said dictum, the amount awarded under the head loss of future prospects does not carry any interest.

opennyai_summary.facts:
This Claim Petition is filed by the Petitioner against the Respondents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by him in the Road Traffic Accident.
Due to the terrific impact, both rider and pillion rider fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately after the accident, the Petitioner was shifted to Lakshmi hospital, for first aid treatment and thereafter he was shifted to Apollo hospital, wherein he was treated as an inpatient.
Due to the accident, he has sustained grievous injuries causing permanent disablement.
The Respondent No.1 is the owner of the offending vehicle and the Respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle and therefore, both Respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the Petitioner.
Despite of service of notice the Respondent No.1 remained absent and he was placed exparte.
In the Objection Statement, Respondent No.2 denied the age, avocation and income of the Petitioner and also denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending car bearing No.KA-02-MQ-4217.
Further, it denies the issuance of insurance policy to the offending Car subject to confirmation.
Further contended that the owner of the offending car has violated the Section 134(c) of MV Act.
Further it contended that the alleged accident has taken place only due to the negligence on the part of the rider of the motor cycle, he rode the same in a rash and negligent manner on a busy road that at 7.45 pm, unmindful of the traffic, resulting in the accident.
Further it contended that the quantum of compensation claimed is highly disproportionate and exorbitant to the facts and circumstances of the case.
Hence, it is not liable to pay any compensation.
